title: Stability Lab — deployment docket and probing plan
content:
TL;DR: personal rollout docket for a cautious, observability-first release of model-v2 variants behind traffic-splits. This is a lab-style plan (low ceremony) meant to be used at the command line and in Slack during the first 72h. Keep it short, act fast, revert faster.

Goals and constraints:
- Primary goal: validate latency and token-cost stability of model-v2-int8 under realistic client traffic while preserving P99 latency SLAs for paid tiers.
- Secondary: detect any accuracy regressions on the three monitoring prompt-sets (search-assist, chat-smalltalk, summarization-short).
- Constraint: no capacity changes for Dedicated pool during first 48h. Use traffic shaping instead.

High-level approach (two-track probing):
1) Probe track: tiny, synthetic cohorts to exercise edge cases and KV cache hot paths (0.1% global traffic). Fast feedback, higher fidelity to edge behaviors.
2) Ramp track: real-cohort slow ramp (0.5% -> 3% -> 10% over ~36h) with tight sentinel thresholds. Real user behavior but gradual.

Cohort definitions and targeting notes:
- probe-cohort-a: internal test clients + 30 beta customers (IDs listed in the beta repo). Always routed via edge region us-west1 to maximize latency variance.
- ramp-cohort-1: 0.5% randomized by user_id hash with sticky cookie duration 24h. Exclude legacy SDK versions < 1.4.
- ramp-cohort-2: move from 0.5% to 3% if all sentinels green for 4 consecutive 15m windows.

Traffic schedule (quick table):
- T0 (00:00): probe-cohort-a only, run 2h smoke tests (latency & cost per token).
- T+2h: enable ramp-cohort-1 at 0.5% for 6h.
- T+8h: evaluate. If green, step to 3% and observe 12h.
- T+20h: evaluate. If green, step to 10% overnight (sleep-safe window).

Circuit-breakers and automated fallback:
- Absolute P99 latency: 1200ms (if exceeded for two consecutive 5m windows -> auto-fallback to model-v1-4b).
- Error rate (4xx/5xx combined): >0.6% sustained for 10m -> instant rollback for the cohort.
- Cost-per-token anomaly: >30% increase vs baseline median (30m rolling) -> pause new cohorts and alert SRE.
- Quality drift (eval-set BLEU/ROUGE delta flagged by metric): automatic throttling to probe only; human review required before further ramp.

Observability and dashboards (quick checklist):
- Pre-deploy: ensure token-level cost traces enabled for model-v2-int8.
- Live: open the "stability-lab" dashboard (link pinned in channel) that shows: per-model P50/P95/P99, request size histogram, token-cost rate, CPU/GPU saturation, KV cache hit ratio, number of scrollbacks.
- Logging: enable debug-span sampling for 1% of requests from probe-cohort-a (adds trace-id header).

Preflight checklist (run 1h before T0):
- [ ] Confirm canary image pinned in artifact registry (sha: replace-before-run).
- [ ] Bake warm caches: replay 10k representative requests on a staging replica.
- [ ] Notify customer-success for beta list and set expectations.
- [ ] Create rollback runbook in channel thread (one-liner commands to flip routing).
- [ ] Ensure permissions: exactly two engineers have ability to flip cohort flags (me + Marco).

Quick commands (personal aliases I use):
- flip-route probe -> curl POST /route/override -d '{ "cohort": "probe", "model": "model-v2-int8" }' 
- rollback-route -> curl POST /route/override -d '{ "cohort": "*", "model": "model-v1-4b" }'
- quick-check: jq pipeline to compute P99 from logs: cat logs | jq 'select(.model=="model-v2-int8")' | ... (keeps changing, add local alias)

What I will watch manually (subjective notes):
- Tail latency spikes that correlate with cache-miss rate (one-off cold-slab evictions show as short sharp spikes). If I see tail latency growth with stable GPU util, suspect serialization or kernel fallback path.
- Subtle token-cost increase that comes from sequence-length growth (clients that started sending longer contexts). Track median prompt length by customer.
- Error pattern signatures: if errors are concentrated on a small set of clients, check SDK version and auth headers. If errors are uniform, look at model library version mismatch.

Version pinning and model family notes:
- model-v2-int8: experimental quantization branch. In artifact registry tag format: v2-int8-20251001-<sha>. Do NOT move default alias until 72h clear.
- Fallback candidates: model-v1-4b (latency baseline) and model-v2-fp16 (higher cost but known quality). Pre-warm both in memory as hidden replicas.

Rollback heuristics I will accept without group call:
- Any auto-fallback triggered by circuit-breakers above.
- Persistent user-facing errors reported by customer-success from >= 5 distinct paying customers in 30m.
- Occurrence of a new systemic failure mode (e.g., model segfault, kernel OOM).

Post-mortem and data capture plan (if rollback):
- Preserve 72h traces and logs (export S3 path).
- Snapshot the token-cost traces and eval-set outputs for the latest 1k requests from ramp cohorts.
- Tag the rollback commit in GitHub and add a short write-up in the PR describing the pragmatic reason.

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Do we want to run a controlled A/B on function-calling flows specifically? A/B could hide quality differences.
- Should we add a client-side SDK flag to force smaller contexts when running in a probe cohort? Low-friction but needs opt-in.
- Verify that on-prem private deployments will honor the same routing override semantics — ping infra-owner.

Personal notes to self (short):
- Keep coffee. Expect to be awake for the 2h, 8h, 20h evaluations.
- If things look fine at 36h, call for a "soft-decision" to move the default alias to v2-int8 but keep fallback window for 7 days.
- Don’t conflate small cost variance with systemic regression. Correlate with request profile.

Appendix: quick checklist for the channel (one-liners to paste)
- "T0 probe started — probe-cohort-a routed to model-v2-int8 (Evelyn + Marco monitoring)"
- "Circuit-breakers: P99>1200ms or error>0.6% or +30% token-cost -> auto-fallback active"
- "Rollback command: /ops rollback-cohort all -> model-v1-4b"

End of docket. This is intentionally terse and action-oriented — use it as a personal runbook during the first 72h and refine into a formal playbook later if we need to repeat the experiment.
